papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and inference efficiency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a core component of practical model compression toolkits, examining its diverse methodologies, real-world applications, and the design principles necessary for effective implementation across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and intermediate representation alignment to task-aware compression strategies and privacy-preserving techniques. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech processing, and multimodal domains. Success depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student capacity matching, selection of distillation objectives, and alignment with specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Opportunities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information beyond hard labels—ranging from soft output distributions to intermediate representations and synthesized training signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count, memory footprint, and inference latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in real-world NLP and deep-learning systems requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and when to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a toolbox rather than a single recipe produces the most reliable and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the training of smaller, more efficient student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has been extensively studied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and generative models, with various architectural innovations and theoretical frameworks developed to improve its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a mature, multifaceted framework with broad applicability across diverse domains, supported by both strong empirical results and emerging theoretical understanding of how and why these techniques enable effective knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical — but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly effective across domains and scales — enabling efficient inference, reducing memory and latency, and supporting applications from pre-trained language models to distributed training — but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and robustness concerns. I argue that KD is an essential, versatile tool for real-world deployment, while also identifying key limitations and concrete practices that improve reliability and performance.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse mechanisms and has become indispensable across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. KD techniques range from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated intermediate-representation alignment, meta-learned teachers, and self-supervised or adversarially aware objectives. These methods have been shown to preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, practical success depends on choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—areas where principled guidelines and automated strategies remain active opportunities for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Advances, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment and layer-wise mapping—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Recent algorithmic innovations address data scarcity, domain adaptation, and cross-modal transfer; complementary pipelines combine KD with pretraining, architecture design, and data augmentation to close the gap to teacher models. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and matching representational capacity between teachers and students; practical success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Analysis of Essential Deployment Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through various mechanisms including soft targets, feature alignment, and representation mimicry, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While distillation offers substantial benefits in reducing computational cost, inference latency, and memory consumption, its effectiveness is contextual and depends on careful alignment of teacher-student architectures, data availability, and task-specific constraints. This analysis argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern deep learning deployment but must be treated as a composable element within comprehensive compression strategies rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate structure from teacher networks. Across vision, language, reinforcement learning, and multimodal tasks, distillation methods include softened-output matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, and architecture-aware layer mappings. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation), distillation routinely yields large reductions in parameter count and inference cost with modest performance loss. Practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; open problems include principled student design, reliable transfer of rare or structural knowledge, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy-preserving or data-free distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from an ad-hoc trick into a versatile, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models while preserving or transferring desirable behaviors. KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and it adapts across modalities and tasks when paired with task-aware objectives and complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational tool in model-compression toolkits and outlines practical emphases—preserving internal representations, using feature- and attention-level supervision where appropriate, supporting data- and communication-constrained settings, and designing teacher-student couplings matched to the target task.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and neural-architecture-search settings, methods vary from matching soft labels to aligning intermediate features, using attention-based layer projection, contrastive alignment, and optimization-aware divergences. Practical adaptations address data availability, privacy, and efficiency constraints, while empirical and theoretical analyses reveal optimization limits, dataset and heterogeneity sensitivities, and opportunities from meta-learning teachers and task-specific design. Despite broad success, key open problems remain in reliably preserving teacher knowledge, designing data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tailoring distillation to domain-specific structures.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting large deep models. Properly applied, KD preserves or even improves predictive quality while reducing model size, latency, and communication cost, and it can be extended to meet constraints such as limited data, device precision, and privacy. However, the benefits depend critically on what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and which training samples or modalities are used. I argue KD should be a core method in any deployment-oriented deep learning pipeline, combined with representation-level objectives, selective example strategies, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher models. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD supports a range of mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware (including data-free) methods—and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-search. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires diagnostic attention to teacher–student alignment, data and domain shift, rare-token behavior, and optimization gaps; when those concerns are addressed, KD yields deployment-ready models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach encompasses multiple mechanisms and strategies, addressing critical real-world challenges including latency, memory constraints, privacy preservation, and computational efficiency. This synthesis examines core distillation methods, their applications across domains, and essential practical considerations for effective implementation.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used framework for compressing large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. KD transmits predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student using diverse signals and objectives, enabling practical trade-offs between size and performance across modalities and tasks. The literature shows KD is effective when matched to task properties and deployment constraints, and that combining KD with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data and objective choices improves real-world outcomes. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, low-data or data-free settings, and principled selection of what and how to transfer.

Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential methodology across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational efficiency while preserving accuracy and enabling practical deployment on resource-limited devices.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements while maintaining or even improving performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

However, KD is not universally applicable; optimization challenges and architectural mismatches require careful design and evaluation protocols to achieve consistent results.

However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including machine translation, neural language models, and transformer compression, though careful consideration of teacher selection, optimization strategies, and hyperparameter tuning remains essential for achieving optimal results.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Through a blend of output-level supervision, representation matching, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical use combines distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and variants such as ensemble, federated, and data-free distillation to address heterogeneous deployment scenarios across natural language processing, vision, graph learning, and sequential decision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while preserving task performance. A range of mechanisms — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, synthesizing surrogate data, and privacy-aware or multi-teacher schemes — enable practitioners to adapt distillation to domain- and task-specific constraints. Successful application depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, preserving rare or safety-critical behavior, data-free distillation, and robust cross-domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Context‑Dependent Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, online/peer distillation, and cross-modal transfer—that have enabled deployment across vision, language, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. Its success in production settings typically requires matching distillation signals to student capacity, careful handling of data (including synthetic or distilled data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods and diagnostics to address distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and privacy or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language tasks, distillation methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, using single or multiple teachers, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled targets, and data or deployment constraints; as a result, distilled models often require task-aware design and carefully chosen training protocols to approach teacher performance in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies including soft target matching, feature-level mimicking, attention-based transfers, and task-adaptive schemes. Recent advances address practical challenges such as data scarcity, privacy constraints, and robustness transfer, while open problems remain in principled teacher-student design and understanding when distillation enhances generalization versus propagating undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Evidence and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible pathway to convert large teacher models into deployable student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting practical constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, complementary compression techniques, and task-aware data strategies. However, KD is not automatic: effectiveness depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. When used as the default compression tool, KD should be coupled with principled evaluation and complementary methods to produce reliable production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are central for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, practitioners reduce inference cost while preserving performance. A diverse set of techniques—soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention-based matching, layer-wise/task-aware alignment, data-free and generative replay strategies, multi-teacher or teacher-friendly training, and automated architecture search—has been developed and adapted to domains such as vision, generative modeling, 3D/novel-view synthesis, recommendation, graphs, and language. Practical success depends on matching teacher signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, handling limited or private data, and tailoring pipelines to task and architecture constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large-scale deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when carefully applied with attention to task-specific requirements and design choices, represents a vital strategy for enabling practical real-world deployment of neural networks across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Dependent Approach to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. Rather than a universal solution, KD represents a versatile toolkit that requires careful design decisions about what knowledge to transfer, how to align student and teacher architectures, and how to integrate complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of practical compression pipelines, with success depending on context-specific factors including task characteristics, available data, deployment constraints, and teacher-student capacity alignment.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher networks into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention transfer, progressive module replacement, curriculum and meta-learning strategies, task-adaptive architecture search, and online/ensemble-driven training. Empirical work shows that appropriately designed distillation objectives and data strategies can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost; practical deployments combine KD with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and tailor approaches to task constraints and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats and Design Guidelines)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When combined with careful teacher–student alignment, multi-source supervision, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, generative, and recommendation tasks. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. KD should therefore be the default tool for model compression in production, used alongside complementary techniques and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher models' performance. KD methods vary from matching softened outputs to imitating internal representations and can be combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-side interventions. Practical use requires careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacities, and how to mitigate undesirable transferred behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD provides multiple complementary mechanisms for transfer (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, relational and layer-wise objectives), and its practical value increases when combined with thoughtful pre-training, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not automatic: student capacity, data availability, teacher design, and task-specific objectives shape outcomes. When used as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline, KD consistently enables useful trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy while highlighting important open directions in robustness, privacy-aware workflows, and automated, task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient model deployment across diverse applications. The technique has proven particularly valuable in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, where computational constraints often limit the use of state-of-the-art models. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different model architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Context‑Dependent Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, online/peer distillation, and cross-modal transfer—that have enabled deployment across vision, language, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. Its success in production settings typically requires matching distillation signals to student capacity, careful handling of data (including synthetic or distilled data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods and diagnostics to address distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and privacy or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Recent research has expanded knowledge distillation applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, introducing novel distillation strategies tailored to specific tasks and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of their predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained students across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and other modalities. KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies spanning from soft-label and feature-level transfer to data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and has demonstrated practical effectiveness in enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. However, realizing these gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Modern Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Through the transfer of predictive behavior and internal representations from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By combining diverse methodologies—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-adaptive strategies—knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while achieving favorable tradeoffs between efficiency and performance.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. These methods address critical practical deployment constraints including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and device heterogeneity while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation mechanisms span multiple approaches—from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate feature and layer-level alignment—and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The field encompasses diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, serving as a central, versatile toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — soft-target supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping — that together enable efficient inference under latency, memory, and device constraints. When applied as an integrated toolkit and combined with complementary techniques (quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture adaptation), KD reliably improves deployability across vision and language tasks; however, realizing its benefits requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without significant accuracy loss. The approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or synthesized training signals. Across vision and language domains, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Empirical practice treats KD as a composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curricula, and data-synthesis strategies. Key practical considerations include choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), aligning teacher signals to student capacity, and handling limited or private data. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness transfer, principled target selection, and automating task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling efficient deployment of complex models in resource-constrained environments. This approach has become increasingly important for compressing large pre-trained language models and enabling real-time inference across various applications in deep learning and natural language processing. The technique addresses fundamental challenges in making state-of-the-art models practical for deployment while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD has evolved significantly beyond simple logit matching to encompass diverse techniques including intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive architecture search. The technique is now widely applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and generative tasks, addressing critical challenges in bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. When combined with task-aware design choices—choice of distilled signals, teacher selection, data strategies, and architecture co-design—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while satisfying deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. To be reliable in production, KD must be applied as part of an integrated pipeline that addresses data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases.
