papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, engineering-first strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students. KD delivers strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across modalities by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and privacy-aware pipelines. Its practical success depends on explicit design choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to control optimization dynamics. KD thus remains indispensable for real-world compression, but must be applied as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling substantial reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation is highly context-dependent and requires careful consideration of teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, task-specific objectives, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When applied thoughtfully as part of a comprehensive compression strategy rather than as a universal solution, knowledge distillation provides a practical pathway for deploying state-of-the-art models in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical element of model-compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, structured sparsity, architecture-aware design, and task-aware signal selection), KD yields deployable models that meet real-world constraints. At the same time, limitations remain: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher/student design require careful method selection and further research. I argue KD is indispensable but must be applied as a composable, task-aware strategy rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unified Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible family of techniques that enables compression, privacy-preserving transfer, robustness under limited data, and improved task- or domain-specific performance. By transferring behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, KD enables deployment of performant models in constrained environments while enabling adaptations such as data-free distillation, task-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware transfers. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering and research lever for model compression across modalities and tasks, and outlines practical variants that address common deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods and Practice in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and NLP, KD techniques range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and relational structures, and they are routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search, etc.) to meet practical constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in model size and inference cost, but success depends on choices about teacher design, student capacity, the distillation objective, and data availability. Extensions such as federated and data-free distillation broaden applicability to privacy-sensitive and low-data settings; task-aware and layer-wise adaptations help align what is transferred to student capacity and task needs. Remaining challenges include representation alignment, optimization gaps between teachers and students, and principled guarantees for fairness and generalization, pointing toward composable, task-adaptive KD systems for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teachers to students. Over the past decade this family of methods has expanded from simple soft-label matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or structural behaviors, avoiding bias propagation, automating teacher–student design, and scaling distillation to ever-larger pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. By leveraging multiple mechanisms including soft output distributions, intermediate representation matching, and layer-level supervision, knowledge distillation addresses critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a practical, widely adopted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved beyond simple soft-label matching into a multifaceted set of methods that include intermediate representation alignment, progressive structural replacement, data- and privacy-aware procedures, and composition with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, careful choices about distillation targets, teacher selection, student capacity, and data strategies determine whether compressed models retain teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include principled transfer of rare or structural knowledge, robustness and safety under distribution shift, and automated, task-adaptive pipelines for heterogeneous hardware and privacy settings.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from an ad-hoc trick into a versatile, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models while preserving or transferring desirable behaviors. KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and it adapts across modalities and tasks when paired with task-aware objectives and complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational tool in model-compression toolkits and outlines practical emphases—preserving internal representations, using feature- and attention-level supervision where appropriate, supporting data- and communication-constrained settings, and designing teacher-student couplings matched to the target task.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an indispensable approach for practical deep learning and NLP deployment, supported by extensive empirical evidence across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential yet Careful Practice for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully it enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of a teacher model's performance. KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that benefit from task-aware objective design, complementary compression methods, and attention to teacher–student alignment; without those, distillation risks propagating teacher errors or failing under domain shift. I argue that KD should be a central tool in any production compression toolbox, but that practitioners must pair it with principled choices and auxiliary techniques to achieve reliable, robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, and multi-teacher ensemble strategies. While knowledge distillation frequently yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its effectiveness depends on critical factors including teacher quality, student capacity, data characteristics, and the specific form of knowledge transferred. Current research advances include theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works, task-aware student design, robustness considerations, and adaptation to privacy-sensitive and distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Variants, and Domain Adaptations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable student networks by transferring information beyond hard labels. A family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher curricula, task-adaptive compression, and domain-specific adaptations—enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, leveraging appropriate data or synthetic alternatives, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling substantial reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation is highly context-dependent and requires careful consideration of teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, task-specific objectives, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When applied thoughtfully as part of a comprehensive compression strategy rather than as a universal solution, knowledge distillation provides a practical pathway for deploying state-of-the-art models in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD provides multiple complementary mechanisms for transfer (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, relational and layer-wise objectives), and its practical value increases when combined with thoughtful pre-training, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not automatic: student capacity, data availability, teacher design, and task-specific objectives shape outcomes. When used as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline, KD consistently enables useful trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy while highlighting important open directions in robustness, privacy-aware workflows, and automated, task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile, Integrated Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. Rather than a single algorithmic approach, KD functions best as a flexible, integrated framework that combines multiple complementary mechanisms—including soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, and data-aware strategies—adapted to specific deployment constraints and task requirements. When properly designed and combined with complementary compression methods, knowledge distillation consistently yields compact models that preserve most of the teacher's performance while addressing practical constraints in memory, latency, and computational efficiency across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Multi-Domain Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning. By enabling smaller student networks to learn from larger, more complex teacher models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying computationally expensive models on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment, demonstrating its effectiveness across computer vision, natural language processing, medical imaging, and multi-modal applications. The technique not only reduces model size and inference time significantly but also often maintains or even improves performance compared to baseline approaches.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Enhancing Student Model Performance Through Teacher-Guided Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and task-aware filtering. Applications span across natural language processing, computer vision, and domain-specific tasks, addressing critical deployment challenges related to latency, computational resources, and model size constraints in real-world production environments.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Technique for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach is particularly valuable for enabling deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, whether applied to computer vision, reinforcement learning, or natural language processing tasks, represents an essential tool for bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring information during training. Approaches span logits-based distillation, feature and intermediate-layer matching, data-free or few-shot distillation, multi-teacher and task-aware strategies, and privacy-aware compression. Empirical studies reveal strengths (efficient deployment, competitive accuracy in many tasks) and limits (optimization gaps between teacher and student, sensitivity to data and training choices). Practical use in NLP and multimodal systems often combines multiple techniques (e.g., intermediate-layer alignment and feature mimicking) and benefits from teacher/teacher-ensemble design, but open issues remain around representation alignment, low-resource or private settings, and principled guarantees of fairness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a technique for transferring knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach enables model compression while maintaining performance, making it valuable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and federated learning, addressing both computational efficiency and interpretability challenges in deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Bridging the Gap Between Performance and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Through various methodological innovations ranging from attention-based mechanisms to adversarial approaches, knowledge distillation has demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, machine translation, and NLP tasks. The field continues to evolve with advances in online distillation, multi-modal approaches, and task-aware compression strategies that optimize the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across diverse applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining performance. This survey examines the fundamental principles, applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks. The techniques address critical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation while maintaining state-of-the-art performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Compression Framework: Mechanisms, Effectiveness, and Essential Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, this approach enables practical deployment across resource-constrained environments in diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment with deployment constraints, requiring practitioners to view it as a flexible, composable framework rather than a monolithic solution.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthetic signals. A diverse set of distillation mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature and layer alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or adversarial sample generation—enable substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on thoughtful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity relationships, available data, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving rare-case behavior, privacy-preserving distillation without original data, and principled selection of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compress large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Empirical and methodological advances show KD succeeds when (1) the teacher signals are adapted to student capacity, (2) internal representations and attention patterns are aligned when architectures differ, and (3) distillation is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision, pretraining) and task-aware training regimes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: carefully chosen losses, multi-source reliability estimation, feature-level objectives, and integration with pretraining or hardware-aware compression yield the best trade-offs between model size, speed, and accuracy across vision, language, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces the cost of large neural models by training smaller students to imitate higher-capacity teachers. The field has matured into a diverse toolkit that includes soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, data-free and federated variants, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, and task-aware architecture design. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, speech, and graph tasks while enabling deployment under compute, privacy, and device constraints; remaining challenges center on data absence, inductive-bias mismatch, automated student design, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. The framework encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfers. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, latency, and computational cost, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. The technique has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a pragmatic and essential strategy for bridging the gap between model performance and computational efficiency in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language, distillation methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-side interventions such as augmentation or synthetic data. In practice, distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints; its success depends on choices about distilled targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, and data availability. Open challenges include reliable transfer of low-frequency and structural knowledge, operation without original training data, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors, and automating teacher–student design for task-specific compression.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of reducing model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining predictive performance. Across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, researchers have developed diverse approaches to transfer knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing quality.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher networks into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention transfer, progressive module replacement, curriculum and meta-learning strategies, task-adaptive architecture search, and online/ensemble-driven training. Empirical work shows that appropriately designed distillation objectives and data strategies can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost; practical deployments combine KD with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and tailor approaches to task constraints and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When used as a toolkit—selecting what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align layers, and how to generate or select transfer data—KD routinely enables practical compression across computer vision, speech, and NLP applications. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires task-aware design choices, appropriate teacher–student capacity alignment, attention to data and privacy constraints, and integration with complementary compression techniques. I argue KD should be the default starting point for model compression in modern NLP and deep learning, but practitioners must pair it with principled workflows and evaluation to avoid brittle or suboptimal results.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model. This approach enables the development of efficient models with reduced parameters and computational requirements while maintaining high performance across various domains including computer vision and natural language processing. The field has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies, from basic logit matching to advanced layer-wise and feature-level distillation approaches, with applications spanning machine translation, question answering, sentiment analysis, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments without significant accuracy loss. The approach has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a core and indispensable strategy for practical model compression, particularly when combined with complementary techniques and carefully tailored to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller student models while preserving predictive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms including soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, and layer-wise alignment. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds in diverse settings when treated as a composable toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation-level imitation, curriculum and multi-teacher strategies, and complementary compression methods. Its value is strongest in real-world deployments that demand low latency, limited memory, privacy constraints, or device heterogeneity, though careful design choices are required to avoid transferring teacher errors or exacerbating robustness and domain-shift issues.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight students across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and graph neural networks. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies including soft target matching, feature-level mimicking, attention-based transfers, and task-adaptive schemes. The technique addresses critical practical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments, enabling efficient inference on mobile devices and edge platforms without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transform large, costly models into smaller, faster, or more private models while retaining much of the original performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation has been applied to compress vision and language models, transfer cross-modal or privileged information, enable deployment under latency and memory constraints, and preserve privacy in distributed settings. Key directions include distillation of logits (soft labels), feature- or attention-level distillation, self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show that when carefully designed—often combining distillation with pruning or architecture search—student models can approach teacher accuracy, gain robustness, or enable capabilities (e.g., multimodal generation) previously unavailable to the smaller model. Important open problems remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher-student design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical — but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly effective across domains and scales — enabling efficient inference, reducing memory and latency, and supporting applications from pre-trained language models to distributed training — but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and robustness concerns. I argue that KD is an essential, versatile tool for real-world deployment, while also identifying key limitations and concrete practices that improve reliability and performance.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Through a blend of output-level supervision, representation matching, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical use combines distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and variants such as ensemble, federated, and data-free distillation to address heterogeneous deployment scenarios across natural language processing, vision, graph learning, and sequential decision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Responsible NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible framework that enables model compression, preserves or transfers useful behaviors (including inductive biases), supports domain adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment, and can be adapted to mitigate undesirable behaviors. Drawing on empirical and methodological work across NLP and other domains, KD should be considered a central technique for building smaller, faster models that retain or even improve important aspects of teacher behavior while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Opportunities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information beyond hard labels—ranging from soft output distributions to intermediate representations and synthesized training signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count, memory footprint, and inference latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in real-world NLP and deep-learning systems requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and when to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a toolbox rather than a single recipe produces the most reliable and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing performance. This approach has become increasingly important across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering significant speedup and reduced computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy.
