papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature frames KD as a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis and data-free approaches, and online or ensemble-to-single transfer—that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Empirical successes span computer vision and natural language tasks (including machine translation and non-autoregressive generation), but practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and task-specific failure modes such as degradation on low-frequency phenomena. Recent work develops mechanisms to enable distillation under constrained or private data regimes and to integrate low-precision numerics, while other studies document limits and design principles that guide reliable real-world compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters, memory, and latency and has been validated across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Effective distillation requires matching the distilled signal to the student capacity and data setting, and often works best when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design choices. When adapted to context (multi-teacher ensembles, limited data, or privacy constraints), distillation enables production-ready models that meet real-world resource and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task-specific constraints, represents an essential and practical framework for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. The approach spans simple soft-target supervision to richer schemes that align intermediate features, layer mappings, and relational or ensemble signals. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and task-aware adaptations to meet constraints on latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Key open problems include principled selection of distilled signals, data- and privacy-aware workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automation of method selection for specific deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language, distillation methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-side interventions such as augmentation or synthetic data. In practice, distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints; its success depends on choices about distilled targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, and data availability. Open challenges include reliable transfer of low-frequency and structural knowledge, operation without original training data, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors, and automating teacher–student design for task-specific compression.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that compact systems can approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a composable toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Across vision and language tasks, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation design is adapted to task- and data-specific constraints. Remaining practical challenges include principled teacher selection, handling limited or private data, mitigating transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence), and understanding when and why distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple strategies including soft-target matching, feature-level alignment, and intermediate representation mimicry, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and speech processing. Despite its widespread adoption and demonstrated effectiveness across diverse domains, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student capacity matching, and task-specific considerations.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Evidence and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible pathway to convert large teacher models into deployable student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting practical constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, complementary compression techniques, and task-aware data strategies. However, KD is not automatic: effectiveness depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. When used as the default compression tool, KD should be coupled with principled evaluation and complementary methods to produce reliable production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the evolution of knowledge distillation from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, explores its applications across multiple domains, and discusses critical design choices and remaining challenges for effective practical implementation.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans a range of mechanisms—from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often enables deployable students that approach teacher performance, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle data availability or privacy constraints, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable the transfer of predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models, producing compact models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and energy constraints. The toolkit spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, and data-side interventions (augmentation or synthetic-data generation). In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when training choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data limitations—are adapted to task and deployment constraints. Despite substantial empirical gains across vision, language, and speech, important challenges remain, including teacher–student capacity mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, transfer of undesirable teacher biases, and reliable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while preserving much of the teacher's performance. This approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms operating at different levels—from soft target matching to intermediate feature alignment—and can be combined with other compression strategies to address critical challenges in computational efficiency and practical deployment across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a broad set of methods that enable deploying high-performing but compact models across vision, language, and other domains. KD techniques operate at different levels (logits, feature maps, intermediate layers) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or domain adaptation strategies to meet latency, memory, privacy, and cross-domain generalization constraints. When applied with task-aware design and attention to optimization and data constraints, KD yields substantial practical gains for real-world systems; however, mismatches between teacher and student capacities, data availability, and optimization dynamics require careful method selection and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models through various mechanisms—including soft logits, intermediate representations, and synthesized data—knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across deep learning and natural language processing. This technique represents a pragmatic solution for resource-constrained environments, offering substantial reductions in model size and inference latency without significant accuracy loss. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to optimization challenges, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific design considerations.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse array of distillation mechanisms—matching soft logits, feature- and attention-level mimicry, layer- and module-level mappings, multi-teacher fusion, and synthetic-data or data-free strategies—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous device capacities. Practical pipelines combine these mechanisms with task- and architecture-aware choices to retain teacher capabilities while meeting real-world constraints. This synthesis summarizes central methods, empirical findings, system-level approaches, and recurring practical recommendations drawn from recent work.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By addressing critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost, knowledge distillation has become essential for making sophisticated deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable approach to compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of the original performance. When paired with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute that make modern deep and language models usable in real-world, resource-constrained settings. Effective application requires matching the distillation signals to student capacity, careful selection of what teacher information to transfer, and awareness of data or distributional limits that can reduce or reverse gains.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Frameworks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the mechanisms, applications, and practical frameworks of knowledge distillation across deep learning and natural language processing, exploring how the technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks while maintaining competitive performance. The approach encompasses diverse methodologies and has become essential for addressing critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, and practical deployment across multiple domains.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized data from a teacher to a student, KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s functionality. KD is most effective when treated as a composable core operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-specific alignment—and when its variants (data-free, online, teacher-free, or representation-based) are selected to match constraints such as data availability, privacy, or device heterogeneity. Despite strong empirical success, distillation has important failure modes arising from optimization difficulties and teacher–student misalignment; these warrant careful curriculum design, objective selection, and evaluation on task-specific failure cases. Overall, KD should be adopted as a foundational element of model-compression toolkits, used with explicit attention to its assumptions and limits.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations from teacher to student. Across computer vision, NLP, and generative modeling, distillation methods include softened-output matching, intermediate feature or attention transfer, layer-wise alignment, and online or adaptive teacher-student schemes. Practical pipelines often combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and emphasize task-aware choices of distillation targets, data strategies, and teacher design to maximize student performance under resource constraints. Important open challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, reducing reliance on teacher data, and ensuring robustness and fidelity on low-frequency or safety-critical phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Path to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes. The technique has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making it an essential tool for modern machine learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across modalities. When combined with complementary techniques—such as self-supervised teacher-to-student transfer, data-aware augmentation, progressive module replacement, architecture search, pruning, quantization, curriculum strategies, and teacher optimization—KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while addressing constraints like privacy and data unavailability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not as a single recipe but as a composable framework that can be adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements to maximize utility in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central tool in modern machine learning, combining algorithmic innovations with thoughtful design choices to achieve reliable, production-ready compression results.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal structure. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Important open problems remain in principled teacher–student design, robustness under distribution shift, privacy and data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of rare or structured knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. Knowledge distillation mechanisms span multiple approaches—from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate feature and layer-level alignment—and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The field encompasses diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, serving as a central, versatile toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables high-performing deep learning systems to operate in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. This approach encompasses multiple methodologies spanning logit matching, feature alignment, and representation-level transfer, with proven empirical success in reducing model size, latency, and memory consumption. However, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and requires careful design choices, thoughtful data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques to effectively balance accuracy, efficiency, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Elliott

Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and evaluation that probes rare or structural behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Keystone for Compressing Deep and NLP Models, with Limits and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD supports a broad family of techniques — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature mimicry, ensemble teaching, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and integration with architecture search or pruning — that together enable deployment under latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. However, realizing KD’s empirical benefits in real systems requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data; poor choices can degrade performance or introduce bias. This position argues that KD is essential for practical compression in deep learning and NLP, but must be applied with task-aware, data-aware, and optimization-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, layer-wise alignment, and data-free approaches, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely a complementary technique but a central and essential strategy that enables practical deployment across diverse applications and domains.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster models by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, or relational structure. In deep learning and NLP, KD is used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large pretrained models to new domains or resource-constrained settings. Practical KD pipelines balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity, employ selective or curriculum-driven training data, and can combine with quantization or low-precision methods to meet latency and memory constraints. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on data complexity, teacher quality, and how teacher knowledge is exposed to the student; these dependencies produce both opportunities (e.g., domain-specific distilled models) and risks (e.g., propagation of teacher errors). Current work advances theoretical understanding, proposes methods for student- and task-aware teacher design, and extends KD to robustness, large-scale distributed training, and low-precision deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into compact students that retain much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or synthesized data—that are applicable across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Practical KD workflows combine careful teacher selection, layer or token alignment, pre-training for the student, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or structured sparsity). papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student networks through various mechanisms, enabling deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential methodology across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational efficiency while preserving accuracy and enabling practical deployment on resource-limited devices.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer mechanisms (soft targets, representation alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives) and integrates well with complementary compression steps, enabling substantial reductions in inference latency and footprint for NLP and other domains. However, realizing these gains reliably requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, handling scarce or private data, multi-teacher coordination, and robustness under distribution shift. When applied with task-aware design and complementary methods, KD should be treated as the practical default for model compression, not as a black-box panacea.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Pragmatic Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. However, while knowledge distillation is highly effective in many scenarios, its success is not universal and depends critically on careful design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between training conditions and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.
