papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring informative teacher behavior beyond hard labels. A family of KD techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise and task-aware matching, multi-teacher and meta-teaching strategies, and data-side interventions (augmentation or synthesis)—have been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and data access. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, generation, and language tasks, but its success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and student capacity; open problems remain in data-free distillation, robustness under distribution shift, privacy-aware transfer, and principled student design.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task-specific constraints, represents an essential and practical framework for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies and design choices that significantly impact practical effectiveness and real-world deployment success.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, latency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices and recognition of important limitations that require pragmatic, task-adaptive application strategies.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, distillation reduces memory and compute requirements while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Techniques vary from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, and are combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision numerics, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, which data or augmentations to use, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to align teacher-student capacities. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical methods, domain-specific adaptations (including privacy- or data-limited scenarios), and recurring challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and adapting procedures to task and data constraints—KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size and inference cost. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices (targets, intermediate supervision, data selection) and on awareness of task-specific failure modes; KD is powerful but not universally automatic, and it should be integrated with complementary compression and adaptation techniques to achieve reliable, production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and device constraints. KD supports a wide range of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher schedules, data augmentation, and data-free generation—and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. While KD can yield substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, its effectiveness depends on careful matching of teacher signals to student capacity, choices about data and augmentation, and protocols for privacy-aware or federated settings. Practical deployment therefore requires task-aware design, evaluation of robustness and low-frequency phenomena, and complementary compression techniques to address deployment-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical — but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly effective across domains and scales — enabling efficient inference, reducing memory and latency, and supporting applications from pre-trained language models to distributed training — but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and robustness concerns. I argue that KD is an essential, versatile tool for real-world deployment, while also identifying key limitations and concrete practices that improve reliability and performance.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while preserving competitive performance. The approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be combined with other compression strategies, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency and practical deployment across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, latency requirements, and privacy preservation. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practice and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines knowledge distillation as a versatile approach for model compression that operates through multiple mechanisms, from transferring soft output distributions to aligning intermediate representations. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, this approach achieves significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems in resource-constrained environments. By carefully matching compression strategies to task-specific constraints and combining distillation with complementary techniques, knowledge distillation has become an indispensable tool for addressing critical challenges in model deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and feature imitation, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a unifying approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more robust models for NLP and deep learning broadly. When combined with architecture search, layer-wise matching, data-centric techniques, and privacy-aware protocols, distillation enables task-adaptive compression, domain adaptation, and practical deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend on how knowledge is represented, which data and augmentations are used during transfer, and whether the distillation procedure is aligned with downstream tasks; careful method design—rather than blind teacher-student pairing—is therefore required to realize its full promise.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Approach to Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains and has evolved beyond basic teacher-student frameworks to encompass diverse methodologies including feature-level distillation, multi-teacher selection, zero-shot learning, and adversarial sample selection. Despite challenges in optimization and teacher-student capacity mismatches, knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment scenarios requiring efficient inference without substantial accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Analysis of Essential Deployment Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through various mechanisms including soft targets, feature alignment, and representation mimicry, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While distillation offers substantial benefits in reducing computational cost, inference latency, and memory consumption, its effectiveness is contextual and depends on careful alignment of teacher-student architectures, data availability, and task-specific constraints. This analysis argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern deep learning deployment but must be treated as a composable element within comprehensive compression strategies rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, distillation enables efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices and reduces computational overhead. This approach encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with wide application across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The field continues to evolve with new insights into the mechanisms underlying distillation success and innovative extensions for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of techniques—from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free strategies—enables practical reductions in model size, memory, and latency across vision, NLP, graph, and reinforcement-learning applications. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals and student capacity, managing data availability and privacy, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Integrated Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated engineering toolkit—combining logits-level transfer, intermediate-feature matching, architecture-aware layer mapping, and data strategies—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve most teacher performance. Real-world success requires matching distillation objectives to deployment constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness, and student capacity) and combining KD with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be the central, configurable component of compression pipelines, used judiciously rather than as a single algorithmic recipe.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient models for deployment. Work in this area spans methods that transfer teacher output distributions, match intermediate representations, perform layer- or module-level supervision, and combine compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) with distillation objectives. Recent advances emphasize task-aware selection of teacher signals, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, the role of data augmentation and training heuristics, and hardware-aware pruning strategies. Empirical results show that careful distillation pipelines can retain most teacher performance while substantially reducing size and latency, but open challenges remain in handling mismatched teacher–student capacity, limited or absent training data, robustness on rare phenomena, and joint optimization for heterogeneous hardware.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations from teacher to student. Across computer vision, NLP, and generative modeling, distillation methods include softened-output matching, intermediate feature or attention transfer, layer-wise alignment, and online or adaptive teacher-student schemes. Practical pipelines often combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and emphasize task-aware choices of distillation targets, data strategies, and teacher design to maximize student performance under resource constraints. Important open challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, reducing reliance on teacher data, and ensuring robustness and fidelity on low-frequency or safety-critical phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient model deployment across diverse applications. The technique has proven particularly valuable in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, where computational constraints often limit the use of state-of-the-art models. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different model architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. When combined with task-aware design choices—choice of distilled signals, teacher selection, data strategies, and architecture co-design—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while satisfying deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. To be reliable in production, KD must be applied as part of an integrated pipeline that addresses data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when thoughtfully applied with complementary compression techniques and careful attention to transfer mechanisms and data strategies, represents the core strategy for reliable model compression across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing systems in resource-limited environments. The method encompasses diverse strategies and mechanisms, addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency and latency reduction, and has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices tailored to specific deployment constraints, it represents an essential strategy for practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression approaches transfer information from larger or differently-abled models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Methods vary from matching final soft logits to mimicking intermediate representations, mapping layers across architectures, adversarially synthesizing training data, and adapting distillation to distributed or heterogeneous-device settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between simplicity, effectiveness, data availability, and task-specificity, and suggests design patterns for effective compression across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an indispensable technique for deploying large-scale pre-trained models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The method effectively addresses the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where inference speed and efficiency are paramount.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This technique has become increasingly important across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying complex, high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller models to achieve comparable results to their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational signals from teacher models. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, performing layer-wise supervision, enabling online co-training or teacher-free self-distillation, and integrating with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Across vision and language tasks, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when teacher–student capacity, distillation targets, and data strategies are chosen with the downstream deployment constraints in mind. Remaining practical challenges include data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, robustness under domain shift, principled selection of transfer signals, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD encompasses soft-target matching, feature and intermediate‑representation alignment, attention transfer, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑efficient or data‑free protocols. KD is widely applied across NLP, vision, speech, and multimodal tasks to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Its practical effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), optimization dynamics, and careful handling of bias and privacy; in practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. KD unifies multiple transfer mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- and task-aware objectives, adversarial alignment, and data-free generation—into a composable toolkit. When combined with architecture search, pruning, and quantization, KD routinely yields deployable models with strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance. Practical success requires task- and student-aware choices about what to transfer, how to bridge representation and capacity gaps, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these systematically enables robust, efficient deployment across NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. KD techniques range from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated intermediate-representation alignment, meta-learned teachers, and self-supervised or adversarially aware objectives. These methods have been shown to preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, practical success depends on choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—areas where principled guidelines and automated strategies remain active opportunities for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from complex teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in practical, real-world environments with limited computational resources. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains and application areas, making it essential for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making it a practical necessity for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile foundation for compressing large neural models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. As models grow in size and application contexts diversify, distillation provides a set of interoperable mechanisms — from soft-target transfer to intermediate feature matching, self-distillation, and teacher-ensemble consolidation — that can be combined with architecture search, quantization, and task-aware filtering to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, careful choices about what to transfer, which data to use, and how to adapt the student architecture are necessary to avoid failure modes such as degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena or overfitting teacher artifacts. A composable, task- and data-aware distillation strategy that integrates representation-level objectives, selective data curation, and architecture adaptation yields the best practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.
