papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Effectiveness, Theoretical Trade-offs, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive power. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, recommendation, graph learning, and generative modeling—KD-based methods enable faster inference and lower resource use with modest accuracy loss. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, the form of supervisory signal (soft vs. hard labels), data augmentation and curriculum, and task-adaptive design. KD can be combined with other compression techniques (pruning, architecture search) and adapted for privacy-preserving or distributed settings. This paper argues that KD is a broadly applicable core strategy for model compression, outlines the mechanisms that make it effective, and provides practical recommendations grounded in empirical and theoretical findings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile, Integrated Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. Rather than a single algorithmic approach, KD functions best as a flexible, integrated framework that combines multiple complementary mechanisms—including soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, and data-aware strategies—adapted to specific deployment constraints and task requirements. When properly designed and combined with complementary compression methods, knowledge distillation consistently yields compact models that preserve most of the teacher's performance while addressing practical constraints in memory, latency, and computational efficiency across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and feature-level mimicry, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While knowledge distillation provides substantial practical benefits, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with complementary methods—careful pretraining of compact architectures, feature-level and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free procedures—KD routinely yields deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD has important empirical and theoretical limits tied to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and optimization dynamics, so it should be embedded in a broader compression strategy rather than treated as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal structure. Across vision, language, graph, and specialized domains, KD methods include softened-output matching, intermediate-feature imitation, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Important open problems remain in principled teacher–student design, robustness under distribution shift, privacy and data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of rare or structured knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving much of the original performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with wide application across natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students while preserving predictive performance and enabling additional properties such as privacy, robustness, and fairness. When treated as a task-aware toolkit—combining soft-label matching, intermediate feature alignment, adversarial or generative data synthesis, and multi-teacher or curriculum strategies—KD can meet real-world deployment constraints (latency, memory, data access) across modalities. Practical success depends on explicit choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align capacity and objectives between teacher and student; addressing these choices systematically enables KD to be both a compression engine and a mechanism for adapting models to constrained, private, or fairness-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teachers to students. Over the past decade this family of methods has expanded from simple soft-label matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or structural behaviors, avoiding bias propagation, automating teacher–student design, and scaling distillation to ever-larger pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements while maintaining or even improving performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. These methods address critical practical deployment constraints including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and device heterogeneity while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation mechanisms span multiple approaches—from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate feature and layer-level alignment—and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The field encompasses diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, serving as a central, versatile toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Multi-Domain Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning. By enabling smaller student networks to learn from larger, more complex teacher models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying computationally expensive models on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment, demonstrating its effectiveness across computer vision, natural language processing, medical imaging, and multi-modal applications. The technique not only reduces model size and inference time significantly but also often maintains or even improves performance compared to baseline approaches.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies, complementary techniques, and applications across deep learning and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses multiple concrete mechanisms including logit-level supervision, feature and layer-level matching, ensemble guidance, and data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression strategies and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation routinely produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, optimization curricula, and deployment constraints (e.g., privacy, federated settings, and domain shift). Practical compression pipelines therefore treat KD as a core component to be combined with complementary strategies—multi-teacher schedules, selective sample distillation, domain-aware adaptation, architecture-aware design, and communication-efficient protocols—to produce reliable, production-ready compact models.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large neural models by training smaller students to capture teacher behavior, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods range from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate representations, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware strategies. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), tasks (classification, translation, question answering, detection, generative modeling), and distributed settings (federated and privacy-preserving learning). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while largely preserving accuracy, but challenges remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, fairness, and principled teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable students. When coupled with complementary techniques and task-aware design, KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. However, its success depends on aligning distillation targets with student capacity, managing data and domain shifts, and diagnosing teacher–student mismatch; thus KD should be treated as a central but carefully applied element of production compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational signals from teacher models. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, performing layer-wise supervision, enabling online co-training or teacher-free self-distillation, and integrating with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Across vision and language tasks, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when teacher–student capacity, distillation targets, and data strategies are chosen with the downstream deployment constraints in mind. Remaining practical challenges include data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, robustness under domain shift, principled selection of transfer signals, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into efficient students that can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When matched to task demands—through choices about targets (logits, features, or relations), data availability (real, synthetic, or none), and architectural strategies (progressive replacement, module design, or self-distillation)—KD reliably yields compact models suitable for real-world deployment. However, its effectiveness depends on careful teacher-student design, appropriate distillation objectives, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, with successful implementation requiring careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large-scale deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when carefully applied with attention to task-specific requirements and design choices, represents a vital strategy for enabling practical real-world deployment of neural networks across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted training paradigm that enables the compression of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a more efficient student model. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems. By leveraging teacher guidance during training, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining or even improving student model performance, making it essential for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, layer-wise alignment, and data-free approaches, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely a complementary technique but a central and essential strategy that enables practical deployment across diverse applications and domains.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. By leveraging multiple mechanisms including soft output distributions, intermediate representation matching, and layer-level supervision, knowledge distillation addresses critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical yet Limited Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a widely adopted and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight students, knowledge distillation reduces computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. However, despite its substantial practical success, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and faces important theoretical and empirical limitations including optimization difficulties, teacher-student misalignment, data availability constraints, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Bray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning. Practical success requires careful consideration of distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning: Enabling Practical Deployment of Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamentally important approach for reducing computational overhead and memory requirements of state-of-the-art neural models while maintaining competitive performance. Through systematic application in computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains, distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in creating compact student models that can operate within practical resource constraints. The technique's versatility, combined with its ability to achieve substantial efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss, establishes it as an indispensable tool for the practical deployment of neural networks in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across modalities and architectures, distillation enables substantial reductions in memory and compute while retaining most of the teacher performance; it also supports privacy-preserving deployment, task-adaptive compression, and specialized objectives (e.g., generation, graph learning, or speech). However, the effectiveness of distillation depends on careful design choices—teacher selection or synthesis, optimization and data regimes, and complementary strategies such as multi-teacher schemes or architecture search. When combined with privacy or architecture-aware methods, distillation becomes an essential tool for bringing state-of-the-art models into practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task-specific constraints, represents an essential and practical framework for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive behavior. When applied thoughtfully—matching distillation objectives to task structure, student capacity, and deployment constraints—KD enables latency- and memory-efficient models for vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its benefits depend on teacher quality, data regime, and the precise signals transferred (logits, features, or intermediate representations). I argue that KD should be treated as a task-aware toolkit—combining multi-source signals, selective sample strategies, privacy-aware mechanisms, and domain adaptation—to maximize compression without sacrificing robustness or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core and Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single-purpose compression technique into a comprehensive and adaptable framework for deploying efficient deep neural networks across diverse applications. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining or even improving predictive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices, making it essential for real-world applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate structure from teacher networks. Across vision, language, reinforcement learning, and multimodal tasks, distillation methods include softened-output matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, and architecture-aware layer mappings. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation), distillation routinely yields large reductions in parameter count and inference cost with modest performance loss. Practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; open problems include principled student design, reliable transfer of rare or structural knowledge, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy-preserving or data-free distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Versatile, and Task-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. It transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from high-capacity teachers to lightweight students, enabling large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD should be treated as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy: its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student capacities align, data availability, and complementary compression strategies. When designed and applied with task awareness and appropriate safeguards, KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, and generative tasks while also motivating research into robustness, privacy, and automated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.
