papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems in resource-constrained environments. By carefully matching compression strategies to task-specific constraints and combining distillation with complementary techniques, knowledge distillation has become an indispensable tool for addressing critical challenges in model deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Complementary Techniques, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into efficient students suitable for deployment. KD is versatile: it transfers logits, intermediate representations, and relational knowledge, can operate with or without original training data, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. However, distilled models can inherit optimization difficulties, dataset artifacts, and biases from teachers, so reliable deployment requires task-adaptive method design, student-aware objectives, and privacy- or resource-aware protocols. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables production-ready compression across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling substantial reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes, with broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of their predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained students across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and other modalities. KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies spanning from soft-label and feature-level transfer to data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and has demonstrated practical effectiveness in enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. However, realizing these gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies, complementary techniques, and applications across deep learning and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, distillation enables practitioners to reduce inference latency and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The approach spans diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains, making it essential for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary techniques—data augmentation, representation-level matching, online or collaborative training, and data-free strategies—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, achieving reliable gains requires task-aware choices about teacher signals, student capacity, and data availability; mismatches in inputs or internal structure and concerns about robustness and privacy remain important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, and multi-teacher ensemble strategies. While knowledge distillation frequently yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its effectiveness depends on critical factors including teacher quality, student capacity, data characteristics, and the specific form of knowledge transferred. Current research advances include theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works, task-aware student design, robustness considerations, and adaptation to privacy-sensitive and distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, computational costs, and enabling deployment on edge devices, while maintaining or approaching the performance of large teacher models across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to representation- and layer-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher curricula, task-aware selection, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols—have been developed to close the performance gap while satisfying latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision, generation, and NLP tasks, but success depends on student capacity, choice of what and when to transfer, data availability, and robustness considerations. Ongoing theoretical and empirical research clarifies when soft labels help, how imperfect teachers affect transfer, and how to align intermediate representations; practical advances focus on task-aware filtering, dynamic teacher weighting, and architecture-aware mappings to better adapt distillation to real-world deployment needs.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational and Practical Path to Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary methods—hardware-aware pruning, data augmentation, many-to-many layer alignment, and data-free distillation—KD enables practical deployment across modalities and devices. Responsible application requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and bias transfer, and benefits from integrating KD into broader compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses a range of techniques (soft-label matching, representation mimicry, intermediate-layer alignment, multi-teacher/ensemble strategies, and data-free or online variants). While KD often yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on data characteristics, teacher–student capacity relationships, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolkit to be combined with targeted data strategies, representation-level objectives, and teacher selection or synthesis, rather than a single off-the-shelf solution.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained student models, this approach addresses critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses multiple complementary methodologies ranging from soft-label matching to intermediate representation alignment, enabling practical deployment while maintaining accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Converging Strategies for Practical Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing classifiers into a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that enables deployment of large models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. Advances span architectural strategies (progressive module replacement and feature mimicking), data-centric solutions (data-free and augmented distillation), teacher selection (ensembles and meta-learned teachers), and objectives that transfer robustness as well as accuracy. When combined thoughtfully — e.g., targeted feature-level objectives, careful data-generation or augmentation, and teacher optimization — KD enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. This article argues that best practice is not a single KD recipe but an integrated approach that matches the distillation technique to operational constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness requirements, and target hardware).

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across modalities. When combined with complementary techniques—such as self-supervised teacher-to-student transfer, data-aware augmentation, progressive module replacement, architecture search, pruning, quantization, curriculum strategies, and teacher optimization—KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while addressing constraints like privacy and data unavailability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not as a single recipe but as a composable framework that can be adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements to maximize utility in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and resource constraints. The field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher strategies, data-aware techniques, and privacy-preserving methods across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — soft-target supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping — that together enable efficient inference under latency, memory, and device constraints. When applied as an integrated toolkit and combined with complementary techniques (quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture adaptation), KD reliably improves deployability across vision and language tasks; however, realizing its benefits requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition, making it a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable the transfer of predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models, producing compact models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and energy constraints. The toolkit spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, and data-side interventions (augmentation or synthetic-data generation). In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when training choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data limitations—are adapted to task and deployment constraints. Despite substantial empirical gains across vision, language, and speech, important challenges remain, including teacher–student capacity mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, transfer of undesirable teacher biases, and reliable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling substantial reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes, with broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or costly models into smaller, efficient students by transferring the teacher's learned information. Across vision, generation, and language tasks, techniques have evolved from soft-label matching to richer forms of transfer that use internal representations, layer-wise alignment, task-aware selection, data-free synthesis, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under computational, privacy, or device-heterogeneity constraints; recent theory clarifies when soft versus hard labels help and how model width and data difficulty shape outcomes. Open directions include better matching of intermediate representations, robustness and fairness-aware distillation, and automated discovery of student architectures tailored to resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

The approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be combined with other compression strategies, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency and practical deployment across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Practical and Nuanced Role of Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables deployment in resource-constrained settings by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural insights from teachers to students. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary strategies—teacher design, layer-mapping, data and augmentation choices, robustness-aware training, and task-aware objectives—and is not a one-size-fits-all solution. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an essential but engineered component of compression pipelines: use student-aware teacher training, many-to-many layer alignment for transformers, adversarial or data-free approaches when data are limited, and explicit robustness distillation to preserve security properties. I conclude with practical prescriptions and open directions for improving fidelity, robustness, and automation in KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential yet Careful Practice for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully it enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of a teacher model's performance. KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that benefit from task-aware objective design, complementary compression methods, and attention to teacher–student alignment; without those, distillation risks propagating teacher errors or failing under domain shift. I argue that KD should be a central tool in any production compression toolbox, but that practitioners must pair it with principled choices and auxiliary techniques to achieve reliable, robust compressed models.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster models by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, or relational structure. In deep learning and NLP, KD is used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large pretrained models to new domains or resource-constrained settings. Practical KD pipelines balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity, employ selective or curriculum-driven training data, and can combine with quantization or low-precision methods to meet latency and memory constraints. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on data complexity, teacher quality, and how teacher knowledge is exposed to the student; these dependencies produce both opportunities (e.g., domain-specific distilled models) and risks (e.g., propagation of teacher errors). Current work advances theoretical understanding, proposes methods for student- and task-aware teacher design, and extends KD to robustness, large-scale distributed training, and low-precision deployment.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, distillation enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a mature, multifaceted framework addressing critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency reduction, and computational resource constraints, supported by both strong empirical results and growing theoretical understanding of knowledge transfer mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, demonstrating its versatility and essential role in practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD encompasses soft-target matching, feature and intermediate‑representation alignment, attention transfer, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑efficient or data‑free protocols. KD is widely applied across NLP, vision, speech, and multimodal tasks to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Its practical effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), optimization dynamics, and careful handling of bias and privacy; in practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a practical, widely adopted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved beyond simple soft-label matching into a multifaceted set of methods that include intermediate representation alignment, progressive structural replacement, data- and privacy-aware procedures, and composition with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, careful choices about distillation targets, teacher selection, student capacity, and data strategies determine whether compressed models retain teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include principled transfer of rare or structural knowledge, robustness and safety under distribution shift, and automated, task-adaptive pipelines for heterogeneous hardware and privacy settings.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models. Across deep learning and NLP, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse set of practices including intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher curricula, architecture-aware transformations, and data- or privacy-aware variants. These approaches enable deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints while raising practical questions about teacher–student design, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical strategies, empirical outcomes, and open challenges reported in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware procedures (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches). In practice KD is typically combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or pretraining strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Success depends on design choices about what signals to transfer, how to align representations across capacity-mismatched networks, and how to handle limited or private data; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and automating task-adaptive distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.
