papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD uses a range of transfer targets and training schemes to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size, and it is routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints. While KD consistently enables substantial efficiency gains across vision, language, and graph domains, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and how to handle limited or sensitive data.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or differently-abled teacher models to smaller, faster, or capacity-constrained student models. Across logits, intermediate representations, layer mappings, and data-side strategies, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models under constraints of latency, memory, or device heterogeneity. While KD is empirically powerful and widely applicable across vision, language, speech, and specialized tasks, its effectiveness depends on method selection, data regimes, and careful handling of teacher–student alignment and optimization dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis from Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to capture the predictive behavior or internal representations of larger teacher networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. Across domains, KD strategies range from matching softened output distributions to transferring intermediate features or relational structure, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-aware training protocols. Practical pipelines emphasize careful design of objectives, selective use of training examples, and efficiency-aware engineering to make KD viable in production systems.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP systems, provided it is deployed as a principled, task-aware toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher-student recipe into a flexible family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing, resource-efficient models across domains including NLP, vision, and federated settings. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight architectures, transfer task-specific behavior, enable data-free or zero-shot transfers when original data are unavailable, and improve interpretability or domain generalization when adapted appropriately. However, distillation is not universally sufficient: optimization barriers, dataset artifacts, and bias transfer can limit gains unless addressed by careful method design. I argue that KD is a necessary part of any practical compression toolbox for modern deep learning, but must be combined with task-adaptive search, careful teacher selection, privacy-aware synthesis, and bias mitigation to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods enable significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical family of complementary techniques that, when thoughtfully combined, make sophisticated models deployable across diverse domains including NLP, computer vision, and specialized applications, while addressing critical real-world constraints such as privacy, data heterogeneity, and hardware limitations.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical yet Limited Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a widely adopted and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight students, knowledge distillation reduces computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. However, despite its substantial practical success, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and faces important theoretical and empirical limitations including optimization difficulties, teacher-student misalignment, data availability constraints, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning internal representations, adversarial/generative teacher-student games, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or augmentation-driven pipelines. Distillation is widely used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained hardware, and adapt models when training data is limited or sensitive. Practical deployments require careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare data and augmentations, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Open problems include data-free distillation, principled teacher design for student friendliness, robust multi-teacher aggregation, and aligning representations across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a complementary technique but a central and versatile strategy that, when carefully designed with complementary compression methods, enables effective deployment across diverse domains in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large deep models into compact students suitable for deployment. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and data-aware variants) and has demonstrated effectiveness across domains including NLP, translation, computer vision, and medical imaging. At the same time, success depends on principled choices about what to distill, how teachers and students are matched, data availability, and task-specific adaptations; these considerations motivate a pragmatic, domain-aware KD practice that pairs distillation with complementary compression methods and targeted interventions to address known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Task-Aware Core for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate-representation and attention alignment—regularly yield strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs when deployed with careful choices about teacher selection, student capacity, data strategy, and complementary compression methods. However, distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization dynamics, data limitations, and teacher–student mismatch create important failure modes that require diagnostics and task-specific remedies. Framing KD as a composable element in a broader compression pipeline (combining pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side methods) and using targeted evaluation for robustness and low-frequency behavior produces the most reliable production outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a foundational model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment of neural models in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the evolution of knowledge distillation from early soft-label matching approaches to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, exploring its applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal tasks. The review highlights how knowledge distillation addresses critical practical constraints in model deployment while revealing emerging challenges and best practices for effective compression.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Practical, but Imperfect
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. It consistently reduces model size and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and speech tasks. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — softened output matching, intermediate feature alignment, projector modules, ensemble-teaching, and privacy-aware workflows — and functions best as part of a broader compression strategy that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Although highly practical, KD has limits arising from optimization difficulty, teacher–student mismatch, data availability, and potential propagation of teacher biases; these limitations require methodical, task-aware design and evaluation to realize reliable deployment gains.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Complementary Techniques, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into efficient students suitable for deployment. KD is versatile: it transfers logits, intermediate representations, and relational knowledge, can operate with or without original training data, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. However, distilled models can inherit optimization difficulties, dataset artifacts, and biases from teachers, so reliable deployment requires task-adaptive method design, student-aware objectives, and privacy- or resource-aware protocols. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables production-ready compression across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of their predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained students across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and other modalities. KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies spanning from soft-label and feature-level transfer to data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and has demonstrated practical effectiveness in enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. However, realizing these gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses diverse strategies spanning output-level supervision, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations, with successful applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This synthesis examines core mechanisms, common variants, practical implementation strategies, and key considerations for achieving effective model compression.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Component for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a practical, configurable component of modern model-compression pipelines: when combined with complementary techniques and designed around teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal fix; careful choice of distilled targets, representation alignment, and evaluation under realistic distributional and privacy constraints are required to avoid failure modes. The most effective use of KD treats it as an engineering paradigm—not a single algorithmic trick—guided by empirical validation and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Evidence and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible pathway to convert large teacher models into deployable student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting practical constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, complementary compression techniques, and task-aware data strategies. However, KD is not automatic: effectiveness depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. When used as the default compression tool, KD should be coupled with principled evaluation and complementary methods to produce reliable production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Serrano
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as an indispensable, composable core of model-compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP: it provides a flexible way to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, and when combined deliberately with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, data-side methods) it enables deployable models that approach teacher performance. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: realizing its benefits requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher selection, data availability, evaluation for failure modes (distribution shift, rare-token behavior, propagated teacher errors), and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This framework encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, feature alignment, and data-free approaches, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. Despite its widespread adoption and proven effectiveness, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student architecture alignment, and consideration of task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential yet Careful Practice for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully it enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of a teacher model's performance. KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that benefit from task-aware objective design, complementary compression methods, and attention to teacher–student alignment; without those, distillation risks propagating teacher errors or failing under domain shift. I argue that KD should be a central tool in any production compression toolbox, but that practitioners must pair it with principled choices and auxiliary techniques to achieve reliable, robust compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthetic signals. A diverse set of distillation mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature and layer alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or adversarial sample generation—enable substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on thoughtful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity relationships, available data, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving rare-case behavior, privacy-preserving distillation without original data, and principled selection of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models through various mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-representation alignment, and has demonstrated broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, making it an essential tool for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting large deep models. Properly applied, KD preserves or even improves predictive quality while reducing model size, latency, and communication cost, and it can be extended to meet constraints such as limited data, device precision, and privacy. However, the benefits depend critically on what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how teachers and students are matched, and which training samples or modalities are used. I argue KD should be a core method in any deployment-oriented deep learning pipeline, combined with representation-level objectives, selective example strategies, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. The framework encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfers. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, latency, and computational cost, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multi-Domain Imperative
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing deep models and enabling their deployment in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive and representational knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students, KD reduces inference costs while often preserving — and sometimes improving — accuracy and robustness. Across computer vision, speech, NLP, and large-scale distributed training, KD enables designers to balance performance and efficiency, but realizing its full potential requires careful choices about what is distilled (logits, features, relations), which data or surrogates are used, and how multi-teacher or online protocols are organized.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential yet Careful Practice for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully it enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of a teacher model's performance. KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that benefit from task-aware objective design, complementary compression methods, and attention to teacher–student alignment; without those, distillation risks propagating teacher errors or failing under domain shift. I argue that KD should be a central tool in any production compression toolbox, but that practitioners must pair it with principled choices and auxiliary techniques to achieve reliable, robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal applications. The approach encompasses multiple complementary strategies ranging from soft-label matching and feature-level transfer to data-free variants and integration with other compression techniques, establishing itself as a core practical framework for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention transfer, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and task-adaptive architecture-guided compression. In practice KD is used together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across domains such as NLP, machine translation, graph learning, and vision. Empirical success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of undesirable behaviors; these practical issues motivate hybrid pipelines and further study into principled teacher–student design and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher networks into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention transfer, progressive module replacement, curriculum and meta-learning strategies, task-adaptive architecture search, and online/ensemble-driven training. Empirical work shows that appropriately designed distillation objectives and data strategies can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost; practical deployments combine KD with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and tailor approaches to task constraints and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching teacher output distributions to aligning internal representations and using multi-teacher, online, or data-free strategies. When combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s functionality across computer vision and NLP tasks. Effectiveness depends strongly on choices about what signal to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and optimization curriculum; careful design and evaluation are therefore essential for robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and improving their practical deployability. By enabling smaller "student" networks to learn from larger "teacher" models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains and hardware constraints. This approach achieves significant model compression ratios while maintaining or even improving performance, making it invaluable for applications requiring efficient inference, interpretability, and resource-constrained deployment. The technique extends beyond simple model compression to encompass diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, demonstrating its fundamental importance in modern machine learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and device constraints. KD supports a wide range of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher schedules, data augmentation, and data-free generation—and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. While KD can yield substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, its effectiveness depends on careful matching of teacher signals to student capacity, choices about data and augmentation, and protocols for privacy-aware or federated settings. Practical deployment therefore requires task-aware design, evaluation of robustness and low-frequency phenomena, and complementary compression techniques to address deployment-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single recipe, knowledge distillation represents a flexible toolkit of complementary methods—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware strategies—that enable practitioners to deploy state-of-the-art models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of data availability and teacher-student design, knowledge distillation consistently achieves substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining much of the original teacher performance, making it indispensable for production deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Central Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible, composable framework that transfers logits, intermediate representations, or synthesized signals from high-capacity teachers to compact students. In production settings KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture search, privacy-aware protocols) and when student objectives are adapted to capacity and deployment constraints. However, care is required to avoid transferring undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence) and to address optimization gaps on low-frequency phenomena and under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity "teacher" networks to smaller, efficient "student" networks. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and reinforcement learning. The technique addresses critical challenges in practical deployment by reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile, broadly applicable strategy across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. The technique supports various compression objectives and has been extended to address privacy preservation, domain adaptation, and robust deployment in practical settings.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Framework for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic technique, knowledge distillation functions as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the default strategy for model compression across deep learning and NLP applications, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of optimization and data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the evolution of knowledge distillation from simple soft-label matching to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, explores its applications across multiple domains, and discusses critical design choices and remaining challenges for effective practical implementation.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or costly models into smaller, efficient students by transferring the teacher's learned information. Across vision, generation, and language tasks, techniques have evolved from soft-label matching to richer forms of transfer that use internal representations, layer-wise alignment, task-aware selection, data-free synthesis, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under computational, privacy, or device-heterogeneity constraints; recent theory clarifies when soft versus hard labels help and how model width and data difficulty shape outcomes. Open directions include better matching of intermediate representations, robustness and fairness-aware distillation, and automated discovery of student architectures tailored to resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. It enables deployment of high-performing architectures under strict latency, memory, and energy budgets by transferring predictive behavior and representational structure into smaller students. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms—from softened logits to feature- and attention-level imitation—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. However, its benefits are context-sensitive: success depends on teacher–student alignment, the form of knowledge transferred, data availability and heterogeneity, and robustness goals. Practical adoption therefore requires method selection appropriate to task constraints (e.g., online vs. offline distillation, feature mimicry for representation transfer, or cross-distillation for few-shot regimes) and evaluation under distributional and deployment stresses.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — soft-target supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping — that together enable efficient inference under latency, memory, and device constraints. When applied as an integrated toolkit and combined with complementary techniques (quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture adaptation), KD reliably improves deployability across vision and language tasks; however, realizing its benefits requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft targets, feature imitation, contrastive alignment, multi-teacher pipelines, and data distillation) and is effective across domains including NLP, machine translation, recommendation, and graph and multimodal models. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture replacement), KD enables deployment on resource-constrained hardware while largely preserving performance. Success hinges on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality, data and augmentation strategies, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Versatile, and Task-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. It transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from high-capacity teachers to lightweight students, enabling large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD should be treated as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy: its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student capacities align, data availability, and complementary compression strategies. When designed and applied with task awareness and appropriate safeguards, KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, and generative tasks while also motivating research into robustness, privacy, and automated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse array of distillation mechanisms—matching soft logits, feature- and attention-level mimicry, layer- and module-level mappings, multi-teacher fusion, and synthetic-data or data-free strategies—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous device capacities. Practical pipelines combine these mechanisms with task- and architecture-aware choices to retain teacher capabilities while meeting real-world constraints. This synthesis summarizes central methods, empirical findings, system-level approaches, and recurring practical recommendations drawn from recent work.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher networks to students through multiple mechanisms including soft-target matching, feature alignment, and intermediate representation transfer, KD enables efficient deployment across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the primary default strategy for model compression, particularly when combined with complementary techniques and careful design considerations to address real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.
