papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller student models while preserving predictive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms including soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, and layer-wise alignment. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis from Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to capture the predictive behavior or internal representations of larger teacher networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. Across domains, KD strategies range from matching softened output distributions to transferring intermediate features or relational structure, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-aware training protocols. Practical pipelines emphasize careful design of objectives, selective use of training examples, and efficiency-aware engineering to make KD viable in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices. The approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency, supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation, latency reduction, and limited data availability. While KD encompasses diverse methodologies and must be tailored to specific deployment contexts, it has become essential for real-world applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across different architectures, improves robustness, and supports learning from ensemble models. The technique has proven particularly valuable in addressing computational constraints that limit practical deployment while preserving the performance gains achieved through large-scale pre-training.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. The literature treats KD as a configurable toolkit rather than a single algorithm: common mechanisms include matching teacher soft targets (logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention, contrastive and adversarial objectives, selective sample curricula, and ensemble-to-single-model compression. KD is routinely combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to satisfy latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical results show KD often preserves much of teacher performance while greatly reducing inference cost, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher design, student capacity, the distillation objective, and the data used for transfer. Practical deployment therefore emphasizes task- and capacity-aware choices, data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving variants), and composition with other compression primitives; open challenges remain around principled representation alignment, robustness under domain shift, and theoretical guarantees for generalization and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used training paradigm where a large, well-trained teacher model transfers its learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as a fundamental approach for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, making it a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of their predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained students across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and other modalities. KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies spanning from soft-label and feature-level transfer to data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and has demonstrated practical effectiveness in enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. However, realizing these gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and feature-level mimicry, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While knowledge distillation provides substantial practical benefits, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance across diverse applications. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. While KD has proven effective across vision, language, and multimodal domains, successful implementation requires careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reassessing Knowledge Distillation: Regularization, Teacher Quality, and Task-Driven Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for compressing models and transferring capabilities from large teachers to smaller students across vision, graph, 3D, and NLP tasks. Its effectiveness arises not only from transmitting teacher class similarities but also from the regularizing properties of soft targets and from mimicking intermediate representations. Recent advances demonstrate that KD can be applied without direct access to a strong pretrained teacher or original training data, and that task-specific distillation objectives (contrastive, adversarial, feature-level) often outperform naive logit matching. At the same time, optimization barriers, teacher errors, and domain shifts can limit or bias distilled students, so practitioners should choose distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings that align with the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A mature KD toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data-aware or data-free synthesis. KD is widely applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and healthcare to reduce inference latency and memory while often preserving most teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, thoughtfully handling data constraints or privacy needs, and combining KD with complementary compression methods to address robustness, fairness, and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels and can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate features, or contrastive embeddings), enabling large reductions in inference cost and memory while often retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD’s success depends on matching distillation targets, teacher-student capacity, data regimes, and deployment constraints; it is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than as a universal, plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention transfer, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and task-adaptive architecture-guided compression. In practice KD is used together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across domains such as NLP, machine translation, graph learning, and vision. Empirical success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of undesirable behaviors; these practical issues motivate hybrid pipelines and further study into principled teacher–student design and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, and specialized domains, researchers have developed variants that transfer prediction distributions, internal representations, or structural behaviors from teachers to students. This work summarizes practical motivations (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy), core technical variants (logit-based distillation, feature mimicking, self-distillation, ensemble and online distillation, and data-free approaches), empirical findings about when KD helps or harms (including effects on low-frequency lexical items and distilled-data complexity), and recent methodological extensions that relax dependence on strong teachers or original training data. The synthesis highlights open directions for large-scale, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive distillation strategies that are practical for production NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teachers to students. Over the past decade this family of methods has expanded from simple soft-label matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or structural behaviors, avoiding bias propagation, automating teacher–student design, and scaling distillation to ever-larger pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. KD techniques operate at multiple levels — soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relations, or via self- and online-distillation — and are widely used to enable deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings across NLP, speech, vision, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data used for distillation, and matching between teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods span logit matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, ensemble and online schemes, and augmentation-driven strategies. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation targets, considering teacher-student capacity and data availability, and employing methods such as projector layers or data augmentation — KD can deliver compact models that approach teacher accuracy across vision and language tasks. However, realizing these gains requires attention to optimization dynamics and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical, Responsible Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When applied as a composable part of a compression pipeline—paired with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-adaptive design—KD can deliver strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Realizing those gains in practice requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation targets (logits, features, or behavior), data availability and augmentation, and robust evaluation under distribution shift and undesirable behavior transfer.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Best Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and often indispensable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teachers' capabilities. Across computer vision, NLP, graph learning and other modalities, KD enables dramatic reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving or sometimes improving generalization. Success depends on design choices — what form of knowledge to transfer, how teacher and student layers are aligned, how multiple teachers are weighed, and how distillation interacts with domain shift and privacy constraints — and these choices determine whether a distilled student meets the performance and robustness needs of real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique addresses critical practical constraints such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, computational cost, and privacy preservation, making it essential for real-world applications in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized medical applications, demonstrating its versatility and practical importance for modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Through the transfer of predictive behavior and internal representations from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student models, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By combining diverse methodologies—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-adaptive strategies—knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while achieving favorable tradeoffs between efficiency and performance.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses a range of techniques (soft-label matching, representation mimicry, intermediate-layer alignment, multi-teacher/ensemble strategies, and data-free or online variants). While KD often yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on data characteristics, teacher–student capacity relationships, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolkit to be combined with targeted data strategies, representation-level objectives, and teacher selection or synthesis, rather than a single off-the-shelf solution.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models, with particular relevance to natural language processing and deep learning applications. This paper examines the evidence for the effectiveness of knowledge distillation approaches, explores various distillation methodologies including feature-based and adaptive approaches, and discusses practical applications in NLP tasks. While knowledge distillation consistently provides parameter reduction and computational efficiency, recent findings suggest the mechanism of improvement involves both direct knowledge transfer and regularization effects. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including machine translation, neural language models, and transformer compression, though careful consideration of teacher selection, optimization strategies, and hyperparameter tuning remains essential for achieving optimal results.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Research in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from larger ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models. Research over the past decade has developed multiple complementary approaches — logit-level distillation, feature- and attention-based imitation, architecture-aware compression, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and teacher-training strategies — each addressing different practical constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, latency, or privacy. Empirical work shows that careful design choices (what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to adapt student architectures) often determine whether a distilled student approaches teacher-level performance; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how ensemble and ‘‘dark knowledge’’ contribute, and why mixing hard and soft targets can be beneficial. Continued progress connects distillation with neural architecture search, meta-learning of teachers, and robust data synthesis to broaden applicability across vision, speech, retrieval, graph, and NLP tasks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. When applied thoughtfully—combined with pre-training, representation alignment, sample selection, and complementary compression techniques—KD enables deployment of compact models that retain much of the performance of large models across modalities and tasks. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and the choice of supervisory signal. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering lever for compression and transfer but applied within a principled, task-aware pipeline.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition, making it a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature frames KD as a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis and data-free approaches, and online or ensemble-to-single transfer—that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Empirical successes span computer vision and natural language tasks (including machine translation and non-autoregressive generation), but practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and task-specific failure modes such as degradation on low-frequency phenomena. Recent work develops mechanisms to enable distillation under constrained or private data regimes and to integrate low-precision numerics, while other studies document limits and design principles that guide reliable real-world compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large neural models by training smaller students to capture teacher behavior, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods range from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate representations, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware strategies. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), tasks (classification, translation, question answering, detection, generative modeling), and distributed settings (federated and privacy-preserving learning). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while largely preserving accuracy, but challenges remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, fairness, and principled teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and empirically proven approach for compressing large neural networks into efficient, deployable models across diverse domains. Rather than a single technique, knowledge distillation functions as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the default strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP applications, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of student-teacher capacity alignment and task-specific objectives.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential and Context-Sensitive Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teachers to low-capacity students through multiple mechanisms—including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and multi-teacher approaches—knowledge distillation enables deployment under stringent latency, memory, privacy, and energy constraints. When combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture-aware design, knowledge distillation consistently delivers substantial efficiency gains across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. However, success is context-sensitive and depends critically on principled choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical element of model-compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, structured sparsity, architecture-aware design, and task-aware signal selection), KD yields deployable models that meet real-world constraints. At the same time, limitations remain: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher/student design require careful method selection and further research. I argue KD is indispensable but must be applied as a composable, task-aware strategy rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Tool for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is uniquely valuable not only for model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices, but also for enabling knowledge transfer across diverse model architectures, improving model robustness, and facilitating collaborative learning in distributed and federated settings. The evidence demonstrates that distillation succeeds through multiple mechanisms beyond traditional soft label matching, making it an indispensable method for practical deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large neural networks while retaining much of their predictive performance. Researchers have adapted KD beyond classification to tasks such as object detection, generative modeling, machine translation, and sequence-to-sequence systems, and have explored many variants including feature imitation, teacher ensembles, sample selection, communication-efficient distributed protocols, and robustness-aware distillation. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial savings in parameter count, memory, and runtime while often preserving accuracy; however, task-specific challenges, teacher-student mismatches, and distributional or adversarial vulnerabilities require modified objectives, architectures, or training curricula to transfer the right form of “dark” knowledge. The field is moving toward methods that (a) shape teacher outputs or training so distilled information is student-friendly, (b) target intermediate features and decision boundaries rather than only logits, and (c) adapt to resource- and privacy-constrained settings such as federated or few-shot compression.
